findings.recorded: Largest B2/B3 cohorts keep identical membership throughout 3–6 s, while relative coordinates change in the original files. Rigid translation/rotation alone cannot explain those changes.
findings.shape_vs_identity: Same-ID particle displacement is not whole-outline displacement. The largest clouds remain comparably compact: median unordered pair-distance distribution changes are only about 0.12/0.10 um, while centered nearest-cloud distances are about 1.93/1.92 um for B2/B3. Internal identity rearrangement is much larger than the change in overall extent.
findings.display: 60x within-group magnification makes micrometre rearrangements conspicuous. 20 ms recorded states appear at 15 states/s under constant 0.30x playback, cross-dissolved into 60 fps. No special rendering branch starts at 3 s.
findings.model: Cycle-averaged forces continue driving independent spheres subject to geometric nonpenetration. No adhesion/fusion model makes a permanently rigid aggregate.
findings.caution: Near-contact dynamics are explicitly unvalidated. Strong near-contact forcing and repeated geometric projections can contribute numerical rearrangement/jitter; this audit does not establish that they are the unique cause or that the movement is physically accurate.
findings.not_resolved: No all-substep motion/projection record or newly completed timestep convergence is available for this late-time motion in this audit. Real physical dynamics cannot be separated quantitatively from numerical artifacts here.
findings.action: No trajectory, force, timestep, radius or group shape was altered or smoothed. Only layout changed in the animation.
